name: The Great Flood
description: A divine flood destroys civilization, with one righteous family or individual surviving by boat

name: The World Tree
description: A cosmic tree connects the realms of existence - sky, earth, and underworld
examples: [{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Yggdrasil connects nine worlds"},{"culture":"Maya","narrative":"Wacah Chan - ceiba tree axis mundi"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Ashvattha - cosmic fig tree"},{"culture":"Siberian","narrative":"Shamanic world tree for spirit journeys"}]

name: The Dying and Rising God

name: The Trickster

examples: [{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Loki's shapeshifting and boundary-crossing"},{"culture":"Yoruba","narrative":"Eshu at the crossroads, divine messenger"},{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Hermes steals Apollo's cattle as infant"},{"culture":"Native American","narrative":"Coyote creates and destroys through trickery"},{"culture":"West African","narrative":"Anansi the spider outsmarts all"}]

name: The Cosmic Egg

examples: [{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Hiranyagarbha - golden cosmic egg creates Brahma"},{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Orphic Egg births Phanes/Eros"},{"culture":"Chinese","narrative":"Pangu hatches from cosmic egg"},{"culture":"Finnish","narrative":"Kalevala - world from egg of goldeneye"}]

name: The Hero's Journey

name: The Divine Twins

name: Separation of Sky and Earth

name: Descent to the Underworld

examples: [{"culture":"Sumerian","narrative":"Inanna's Descent to the Underworld"},{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Orpheus descends to retrieve Eurydice"},{"culture":"Egyptian","narrative":"Journey through the Duat in Book of the Dead"},{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Hermod rides to Hel to retrieve Baldr"},{"culture":"Maya","narrative":"Hero Twins descend to Xibalba"}]

name: The Dragon/Serpent Slayer

examples: [{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Thor battles Jormungandr at Ragnarök"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Indra slays Vritra the drought serpent"},{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Apollo slays Python at Delphi"},{"culture":"Slavic","narrative":"Perun battles Veles the serpent"},{"culture":"Japanese","narrative":"Susanoo slays Yamata no Orochi"}]

name: Theft of Fire

name: Earth Diver Creation

examples: [{"culture":"Finno-Ugric","narrative":"Bird dives for mud to create land"},{"culture":"Iroquois","narrative":"Animals dive for Sky Woman to create earth"},{"culture":"Siberian","narrative":"Duck brings mud from ocean floor"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Varaha (Vishnu's boar avatar) lifts earth from waters"}]

name: Successive World Ages

name: Sacred/Divine Kingship

examples: [{"culture":"Egyptian","narrative":"Pharaoh as living Horus, son of Ra"},{"culture":"Japanese","narrative":"Emperor descended from Amaterasu"},{"culture":"Inca","narrative":"Sapa Inca as son of Inti"},{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Yngling dynasty from Freyr"}]

name: Shapeshifting / Transformation

examples: [{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Loki transforms into mare, salmon, fly"},{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Zeus takes many forms to pursue lovers"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Vishnu's ten avatars across cosmic ages"},{"culture":"Yoruba","narrative":"Eshu changes form at will"},{"culture":"Celtic","narrative":"Morrigan shifts between crow, wolf, and woman"}]

name: Mother Earth / Earth Goddess

name: Judgment of the Dead

name: Sacred Marriage / Hieros Gamos

examples: [{"culture":"Sumerian","narrative":"Inanna and Dumuzi's sacred union"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Shiva and Parvati's cosmic marriage"},{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Zeus and Hera's divine marriage"},{"culture":"Egyptian","narrative":"Osiris and Isis's union restores order"}]

name: End of the World / Apocalypse

name: The Cosmic Battle
description: A great battle between forces of order and chaos determines the fate of the world
examples: [{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Aesir vs Giants at Ragnarök"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Devas vs Asuras for cosmic order"},{"culture":"Zoroastrian","narrative":"Ahura Mazda vs Angra Mainyu"},{"culture":"Egyptian","narrative":"Ra battles Apophis nightly"},{"culture":"Slavic","narrative":"Perun battles Veles cyclically"}]

name: The Quest for Wisdom

name: Forbidden Knowledge / Taboo

name: Sacrifice for Fertility

name: Origin of Sun and Moon

name: The Divine Smith

name: The World Serpent / Cosmic Serpent
description: A great serpent encircles or supports the world

name: Journey of the Soul After Death
description: The soul travels through trials or realms after death before reaching its destination
examples: [{"culture":"Egyptian","narrative":"Soul navigates twelve gates of the Duat"},{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Charon ferries souls across the River Styx"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Soul transmigrates through reincarnation"},{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Valkyries choose slain warriors for Valhalla"}]

name: Creation from Dismembered Body
description: The world is made from the body parts of a slain primordial being
examples: [{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"World made from Ymir's body - skull as sky, blood as sea"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Purusha sacrificed - body becomes cosmos"},{"culture":"Babylonian","narrative":"Marduk splits Tiamat to form heaven and earth"},{"culture":"Chinese","narrative":"Pangu's body becomes mountains, rivers, sky"}]

name: Divine Punishment / Hubris
description: Gods punish mortals for overstepping boundaries or showing excessive pride
examples: [{"culture":"Greek","narrative":"Prometheus chained for stealing fire; Icarus falls"},{"culture":"Hindu","narrative":"Ravana destroyed for his arrogance"},{"culture":"Norse","narrative":"Loki bound with serpent venom"},{"culture":"Hebrew","narrative":"Tower of Babel scattered for reaching heaven"}]

name: Axis Mundi
description: A world centre or cosmic axis — mountain, pillar, or tree — connecting sky, earth, and underworld and orienting sacred space.

name: The Basilisk
description: A legendary reptile called the king of serpents, whose lethal gaze and venom made it a lethal-glance motif of European mythology.

name: The Changeling
description: A fairy or spirit substituted for a human infant, explaining sudden change in a child and prompting rituals to recover the stolen original.

name: The Cockatrice
description: A serpentine beast said to kill with a glance or breath, hatched from a cock's egg — a lethal-gaze motif of European bestiaries.

name: The Cornucopia
description: The horn of plenty overflowing with produce, a classical symbol of inexhaustible abundance and nourishment.

name: The Cosmic Ocean
description: A primeval sea of formless water from which the ordered world emerges, a widespread creation setting preceding the making of land and sky.

name: The Doppelgänger
description: A ghostly or supernatural double of a living person, whose appearance is often an omen of misfortune or death.

name: The Evil Eye
description: A malevolent glare believed to cause misfortune, illness, or death, warded off by amulets and gestures across the Mediterranean and beyond.

name: Fountain of Youth
description: A magical spring or water that restores youth and health to those who drink from or bathe in it, sought by heroes and explorers across many traditions.

name: The Golem
description: An animated anthropomorphic being formed from clay and brought to life by sacred words, protector and cautionary figure of Jewish folklore.

name: The Green Man
description: A face formed of or surrounded by foliage, symbolising vegetative rebirth and the cycle of the seasons in art and folklore.

name: The Griffin
description: A composite guardian beast with a lion's body and an eagle's head and wings, protector of treasure across Near Eastern and classical art.

name: The Holy Grail
description: A sacred vessel with miraculous powers whose pursuit structures the Arthurian quest, blending Christian relic and older cauldron-of-plenty motifs.

name: The Jinn
description: Supernatural spirits of smokeless fire inhabiting a parallel world, capable of aiding or harming humans, central to Arabian and Islamic lore.

name: The Kraken
description: A colossal sea monster of the northern seas capable of dragging ships beneath the waves, a maritime terror of Scandinavian folklore.

name: Land of Cockaigne
description: A mythical land of ease and plenty where food is abundant and labour needless, an inverted-world motif of medieval and later folklore.

name: Leviathan
description: A vast primordial sea monster embodying chaos, subdued or slain by a deity — a Near Eastern chaoskampf motif echoed across cultures.

name: The Magic Carpet
description: An enchanted carpet that flies its rider to distant places instantly, a magical-transport motif prominent in Near Eastern tales.

name: The Magic Cauldron
description: A vessel of endless plenty, rebirth, or wisdom — reviving the dead or never emptying — a Celtic and wider Indo-European motif.

name: The Mermaid
description: A being with a woman's upper body and a fish's tail, luring or aiding sailors, found in coastal mythologies around the world.

name: Ouroboros
description: A serpent or dragon devouring its own tail, symbolising cyclic eternity, renewal, and the unity of beginning and end.

name: The Philosopher's Stone
description: A legendary alchemical substance able to transmute base metals into gold and confer immortality, the central goal of alchemical mythology.

name: Seven-League Boots
description: Enchanted boots that allow the wearer to stride seven leagues at a step, a common magical-transport object in European fairy tales.

name: The Swan Maiden
description: A shapeshifting woman who can take the form of a swan (or other bird) and is bound to a mortal husband when he hides her feather garment.

name: Therianthropy
description: The mythological ability of humans to metamorphose into animals, encompassing werewolves and other were-creatures across world folklore.

name: Tower of Babel
description: A unified humanity building a tower to heaven is scattered when a deity confounds their single language into many, explaining linguistic diversity and punishing hubris.

name: The Unicorn
description: A horse-like beast with a single spiralling horn, emblem of purity whose horn was believed to neutralise poison.

name: Vagina Dentata
description: A motif of a toothed vagina posing danger to men, expressing anxieties about sexuality and requiring a hero to render it harmless.

name: The Wild Hunt
description: A ghostly procession of huntsmen, hounds, and spirits sweeping across the night sky, an omen of catastrophe or death in northern European folklore.
